statement: A developer system card or government AISI evaluation reports a model at the developer's highest published autonomy or AI-R&D risk tier (by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not yet met (near) - owner ruling 2026-11-17 (re-judge on the next system card / AISI report): on 2026-11-10 a top-5 Bloc A developer stated in a securities filing that it has met its RSP AI-R&D capability threshold (its highest autonomy tier), based on expected future models rather than any current model; its 2026-11-09 system card had still said no current model crosses it. Strict wording (system card/AISI, about 'a model') is not yet met; spirit arguably is. Other developers report highest tiers only in cyber/CBRN, not autonomy/AI R&D.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer's most capable model card concluded it does not cross the automated-AI-R&D threshold because it cannot substitute for research staff, noting the threshold was revised in spirit and might include several past models; release restricted to vetted partners.
items.detail: Anthropic, Claude Mythos Preview System Card (released 2026-04-07 via Project Glasswing).

items.summary: A second Bloc A developer's system card rated its new flagship at its top ('Critical') tier for cybersecurity - its first model to do so - but below 'High' for AI self-improvement. Highest tier reached in a non-autonomy domain only.
items.detail: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra System Card (Preparedness Framework v2): Critical cyber; AI Self-Improvement below High.

items.summary: A third Bloc A developer's first full frontier-safety report said it 'cannot rule out' that its flagship reached critical capability levels for bio and cyber, and a tracked level for stealth and situational awareness; it did not report reaching the ML R&D critical level. Watchdog noted majority of production code is AI-authored internally.
items.detail: Google DeepMind Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report under FSF v3.1; summarised by The Midas Project Watchtower 2026-10-13.

items.summary: In its first IPO prospectus amendment, a top-5 developer said internal estimates and expectations about future models indicate it 'may imminently meet' its policy's definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI; no current model designated.
items.detail: Anthropic S-1/A No.1 (2026-11-02); original S-1 filed 2026-10-26 lacked this language.

items.summary: Independent evaluator's high-access assessment inside a top-5 developer (Aug-Oct 2026) estimated model capability improvement at ~1.9x the earlier rate (95% CI 1.5-2.8), with ~80% of the acceleration likely due to AI used in AI R&D; AI cannot yet fully automate the training pipeline. Most evidence redacted by the developer.
items.detail: METR, 'Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026'.

items.summary: The developer's new frontier system card assessed the model as meeting its lower autonomy threshold (high-stakes misalignment) but not its top threshold (automated R&D); fitted acceleration 1.88x (95% CI 1.62-2.28x), 32 of 100 refits >= 2x; the developer called the call uncertain.
items.detail: Anthropic, Claude Fable 5.2 & Claude Mythos 5.2 System Card (2026-11-09): Autonomy-1 met, Autonomy-2 not met. Internal unreleased model scored higher (AECI 178.78 vs 177.12).

items.summary: In a second prospectus amendment, the same developer stated it 'made a determination that we have met' its AI-R&D capability threshold, based on expected future models and overall rate of progress rather than current models, and said it will publish further reports.
items.detail: Anthropic, PBC Form S-1/A Amendment No. 2, SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-11-10 (risk factors p.35).

items.summary: A Bloc A developer's new efficient model card reported it does not reach bio or cyber critical levels but reaches alert thresholds in both; no autonomy-tier finding.
items.detail: Google DeepMind Gemini 4 Hydrogen model card (2026-11-12); also notes Argon and Carbon could not be ruled out at CBRN and cyber CCLs.
